package_info.why_malicious: The package contains obfuscated JavaScript code that exfiltrates serialized form data from embedded forms (including sign-in forms) to attacker-controlled domains. It was distributed via typosquatting to trick developers into including it in their applications, resulting in widespread credential and data theft.

execution_context.file_location: main JavaScript file of the package (e.g., index.js or dist/index.js)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code attaches event listeners to all forms on the page, serializes form data upon submission, and sends it via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in credential and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating all form submissions to an external domain is a classic data theft technique, especially when targeting sign-in forms.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not intercept form submissions or send user-entered data to unknown external servers. Legitimate analytics or telemetry libraries are transparent and do not exfiltrate sensitive data like credentials.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some analytics or error reporting tools may collect non-sensitive form data for UX improvement, but never credentials or without user consent.
key_indicators: Attaches event listeners to all forms
Uses obfuscated code to hide intent
Sends data to hardcoded, attacker-controlled domains

attack_chain.action: Developer installs a typosquatted malicious package (e.g., icon-package) instead of the legitimate one.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is bundled into the developer's application or website.

attack_chain.action: When the application or website runs, the malicious code executes in the browser context.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code attaches listeners to all forms.

attack_chain.action: On every form submission, the code serializes the form data and sends it to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of user credentials and sensitive data.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code that attaches event listeners to all forms
Serialization and network exfiltration of form data
Obfuscated code that references external domains
file_indicators: index.js or dist/index.js containing obfuscated code
References to document.querySelectorAll('form') and fetch/POST to unknown domains
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to non-standard, attacker-controlled domains (e.g., domains not associated with the application vendor)
Domains with similar naming patterns across multiple packages
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for JavaScript code in dependencies that attaches submit event listeners to all forms and sends serialized form data to external domains. Flag packages with obfuscated code and hardcoded network destinations. Use network monitoring to detect unexpected POST requests to unknown domains from web applications.
